<!-- coderabbit:state {"thread":"41f0c2","round":2} -->
_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

`ReadBudget` returns `os.ReadFile`'s error untouched, so a caller that reads
three budgets cannot tell which one is missing. Wrap it with the path.

| Newer run | Older run | Outcome |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| prod | prod | The workflow group cancels the older run |
| prod | stage | Prod cancels the running job, the loser posts CANCELLED |

<details>
<summary>🔎 Supported by static analysis</summary>

🏁 Script executed:

```shell
#!/bin/bash
set -eu
printf '%s\n' '--- callers of ReadBudget ---'
rg -n --no-heading 'ReadBudget\(' -g '!*_test.go' .
printf '%s\n' '--- the function itself ---'
sed -n '15,32p' testdata/fixture/sample.go
printf '%s\n' '--- every bare return of an os error ---'
rg -n 'return 0, err$' testdata
printf '%s\n' '--- done ---'
```

Repository: KyleKing/second-look

Length of output: 47492

---

🌐 Web query:

`go wrap os.ReadFile error with path fmt.Errorf %w convention`

💡 Result:

The convention is to wrap with the operation and the operand, so the message
reads as a sentence when the caller adds its own. See the errors package
documentation for what `%w` promises about `errors.Is`.
</details>

<!-- end of coderabbit comment -->

notes.author: KyleKing
notes.body: Agreed. Wrapping with the path, not the call.
